papers.claim: Linear bandits with k actions, horizon n and misspecification eps: regret of order sqrt(d n log k) + eps n sqrt(d) log n. This is sqrt(dT log K) when well specified, giving d^{1/2} and matching the sqrt(dT) lower bound up to log factors.

papers.title: No-Regret Linear Bandits under Gap-Adjusted Misspecification
papers.claim: Search snippet only (fetched PDF was unreadable binary): restates the Lattimore et al. 2020 phased elimination bound O(sqrt(dT log(|A| log T/delta)) + eps sqrt(d) T log T) under uniform misspecification.

triage.summary: The gap is a sqrt(log K) factor between the upper bound O(sqrt(dT log K)) (Bubeck-Cesa-Bianchi-Kakade 2012) and the lower bound Omega(sqrt(dT)), with no K dependence. I found no published lower bound of Omega(sqrt(dT log K)) for a fixed finite action set with [0,1] rewards, and no paper that explicitly calls the problem open. Closest results: (1) Tajdini, Scarlett and Jamieson (arXiv 2506.04775), Theorem 2, give the 'first n-dependent' lower bound for a fixed set of at most n actions with n in [d, 2^{d/4}]. At eps=1 it reads Omega(sqrt(dT log n / log d)) (my specialisation). Their reward is a scaled Bernoulli taking the value about 1/gamma, so it is not in [0,1], and a log d factor is still missing. (2) Ito (NeurIPS 2024) claims O(sqrt(dT log(K min{1,S/d}))) for contextual linear bandits with S contexts 'together with a matching lower bound'. With S=1 this would be about sqrt(dT log(K/d)) for a fixed set, but I couldn't read either PDF (OpenReview, NeurIPS), so I couldn't check whether the lower bound holds for S=1 or for bounded rewards; this paper should be checked next. Li, Wang and Zhou (COLT 2019) prove Omega(sqrt(dT log T log n)), but only for action sets that change every round. On the hypercube {-1,1}^d, where K=2^d, Bubeck's informal slides say sqrt(dn log|A|) is tight, which shows log K is needed only at that extreme.

papers.title: Improved Regret Bounds for Linear Bandits with Heavy-Tailed Rewards
papers.claim: Theorem 2: for n in [d, 2^{floor(d/4)}] there is a fixed action set with |A| <= n and heavy-tailed (scaled Bernoulli) rewards with regret Omega(T^{1/(1+eps)} d^{eps/(1+eps)} (log n / log d)^{eps/(1+eps)}). At eps=1 this is about sqrt(dT log n / log d), but the rewards are not in [0,1]. The paper calls it the first n-dependent lower bound.

papers.title: On the Minimax Regret for Contextual Linear Bandits and Multi-Armed Bandits with Expert Advice
papers.claim: Abstract: an algorithm achieving O(sqrt(dT log(K min{1, S/d}))) for contextual linear bandits with context-space size S, together with a matching lower bound. I could not verify whether the lower bound applies with S=1 or to [0,1] rewards.

papers.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linearly Parameterized Bandits
papers.claim: Lower bound Omega(sqrt(dT log T log n)) for n <= 2^{d/2} actions per round, in a contextual setting where the action set changes every round, so not a fixed set.

papers.title: Towards Minimax Policies for Online Linear Optimization with Bandit Feedback
papers.claim: Exponential weights with John's-ellipsoid exploration gives regret of order sqrt(dn log N) for N actions. Bubeck's slides say this is unimprovable without further assumptions, with tightness for the hypercube {-1,1}^d.

triage.summary: The polynomial gap in d (upper d^1 from Dani et al. 2008, lower d^0.5 from MAB embeddings) is a database artifact. Finite action sets already have lower bounds that grow to Omega(d sqrt T). (1) The hypercube {-1,1}^d is a finite action set (2^d actions), and the standard Assouad argument (Lattimore-Szepesvari 2020, Ch. 24) gives Omega(d sqrt T). I saw this only through secondary sources citing the book; I did not fetch the book or confirm the theorem number. Scaling to the unit l2 ball changes constants, not the rate. (2) Li, Wang & Zhou (COLT 2019) prove Omega(sqrt(dT log T log n)) for n <= 2^{d/2} actions. With n = 2^{d/2} this is Omega(d sqrt(T log T)). Their VCL-SupLinUCB upper bound matches it up to iterated-log factors. Caveat: their setting is contextual, and the abstract does not say whether the lower-bound construction needs time-varying action sets; the fixed-hypercube bound covers the d-exponent anyway. If K is tracked separately, Chu et al. 2011 (SupLinUCB upper O(sqrt(Td ln^3(KT ln T/delta))), lower Omega(sqrt(Td))) and phase elimination with G-optimal design (LS book Thm 22.1, seen only via secondary descriptions) give sqrt(dT log K)-type rates. So the d-exponent is settled up to logs. Only log factors in T remain; I did not find a result settling the extra sqrt(log T) for fixed (non-contextual) action sets.

papers.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linearly Parameterized Bandits (Li, Wang, Zhou, COLT 2019)
papers.claim: For n <= 2^{d/2} actions per period, minimax regret is Omega(sqrt(dT log T log n)); VCL-SupLinUCB matches this up to iterated log factors. The setting is contextual; the abstract does not say whether the lower bound needs time-varying action sets.

papers.title: Contextual Bandits with Linear Payoff Functions (Chu, Li, Reyzin, Schapire, AISTATS 2011)
papers.claim: SupLinUCB regret O(sqrt(Td ln^3(KT ln T/delta))) with probability 1-delta; lower bound Omega(sqrt(Td)).

papers.title: Bandit Algorithms (Lattimore, Szepesvari) - Ch. 22 phase elimination, Ch. 24 hypercube lower bound
papers.claim: Seen only through secondary sources citing the book, not fetched directly. Phase elimination with G-optimal design gives about sqrt(dT log(KT)) for finite action sets (Thm 22.1); the hypercube {-1,1}^d (finite) lower bound gives Omega(d sqrt T) (Ch. 24; exact theorem number not confirmed).

triage.summary: The polynomial gap in d is closed. A non-degenerate ellipsoid maps linearly to the unit ball, and the parameter set stays bounded. For the unit ball, Rusmevichientong & Tsitsiklis (2010) prove a lower bound of order d√T for any policy, which is stronger than the database's best lower bound of √(dT). Banerjee & Gopalan (2023) claim an optimal lower bound for a wide class of convex action spaces; a search summary says this extends the construction to ℓ_p balls, but I only saw the abstract. Upper bounds are already linear in d: Dani et al. (2008) give d√T·polylog, and OFUL (Abbasi-Yadkori et al. 2011) improves the log factors to d√T·polylog T (summarised as almost matching Ω(d√n); I did not confirm the exact log power). So the minimax rate is d√T up to logarithmic factors. A gap of up to about log T in T remains. The log-free phased policy of Rusmevichientong & Tsitsiklis reportedly scales as ‖θ‖+1/‖θ‖ (third-party summary; the PDF fetch failed), so it is not uniform over the parameter set. I found no paper removing the last log factor in the worst case, and none stating that this is open.

papers.title: Linearly Parameterized Bandits
papers.claim: For arms on the unit sphere, regret and Bayes risk are Θ(r√T), with a lower bound for any policy. A phased explore/exploit policy is the upper bound (reportedly scaling with ‖θ‖+1/‖θ‖ per a third-party summary). For general arm sets, an upper bound of O(r√T log^{3/2} T).

papers.title: On the Minimax Regret for Linear Bandits in a wide variety of Action Spaces
papers.claim: Abstract claims an optimal regret lower bound for a wide class of convex action spaces. A search summary says this extends the d√T lower-bound construction to ℓ_p balls with 1<p<∞; I only saw the abstract, which states no formulas.

papers.title: Improved Algorithms for Linear Stochastic Bandits
papers.claim: OFUL improves the regret bound of earlier confidence-ellipsoid methods by a logarithmic factor. A lecture summary gives O(d√n·polylog n), almost matching the Ω(d√n) lower bound; exact log power not confirmed.

triage.summary: Not closed for a fixed, arbitrary compact action set, but the gap is narrower than the database shows. Upper bound: Zimmert & Lattimore (COLT 2022) prove O(d√(T log T)) for adversarial linear bandits on general action sets. That beats the database's Dani et al. bound, which grows like d·√T·log^1.5 T. It should carry over to the stochastic setting with bounded rewards; with sub-Gaussian noise it needs a truncation step that I did not check. Lower bound: Ω(d√T) is still the best for a fixed set. Li, Wang & Zhou state Ω(d√(T log T)) for infinite action sets with a matching upper bound up to log log T. The arXiv abstract covers only finite sets; the infinite-set claim comes from a seminar page, which calls it a corollary of the finite-set bound with n ≤ 2^(d/2) candidate actions per round. Their setting is contextual, and my assumption (not confirmed) is that the construction needs the action set to change each round, so it would not apply here. For ellipsoids, including the unit ball, Zhang, Hadiji & Combes (2025) show Θ(dσ√T) up to a universal constant, so no log factor is needed there. The remaining question is whether a √(log T) factor is needed in the worst case over fixed compact sets. Banerjee & Gopalan (2023) cite Lattimore & Szepesvári as calling the characterisation of minimax regret across action spaces an open problem. I found no source naming this specific log factor as open and did not check the book itself, so 'open_known' is somewhat hedged.

papers.title: Return of the bias: Almost minimax optimal high probability bounds for adversarial linear bandits
papers.claim: Zimmert & Lattimore: O(d√(T log T)) regret for adversarial linear bandits on general action sets, against an adaptive adversary and with high probability. This improves the Dani et al. upper bound for this setting, assuming the adversarial-to-stochastic transfer holds.

papers.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linearly Parameterized Bandits
papers.claim: Li, Wang & Zhou, linear contextual bandits. arXiv abstract (finite sets, n ≤ 2^(d/2) actions per round): minimax regret Ω(√(dT log T log n)), matched up to iterated logs. A seminar page adds: O(√(d²T log T))·poly(log log T) upper and matching Ω(√(d²T log T)) lower bound for infinite sets, derived from the finite-set bound. Whether the lower bound needs a changing action set was not confirmed; assumed not to apply to a fixed set.

papers.title: Linear Bandits on Ellipsoids: Minimax Optimal Algorithms
papers.claim: Zhang, Hadiji & Combes: minimax regret Θ(dσ√T + d‖θ‖) on ellipsoidal action sets up to a universal constant, so no log factor for this subclass.

papers.title: On the Minimax Regret for Linear Bandits in a wide variety of Action Spaces
papers.claim: Banerjee & Gopalan cite Lattimore & Szepesvári as calling the minimax regret of linear bandits across action spaces an open problem, and give an optimal lower bound for a wide class of convex action spaces.

triage.summary: The gap is closed. For stochastic linear bandits on the unit ball with subgaussian noise, the minimax regret is Θ(dσ√T). Lower bound: Lattimore & Szepesvári, Bandit Algorithms (2020), Theorem 24.2 / Section 24.2, gives Ω(d√T) for the unit ball. This is stronger than the √(Td) bounds in the database. I did not see the book's text directly; the claim comes from papers that cite and restate it (arXiv:2301.03597, arXiv:2003.00153, arXiv:2601.23164). Upper bound: Zhang, Hadiji & Combes (arXiv:2502.17175, 2025), Theorem 3.1 / Corollary 3.1. Their E2TC algorithm handles centered ellipsoids, including the unit ball (A=I), with noise that is subgaussian with variance proxy σ². It needs σ and T but no bound on ‖θ‖. The bound is R_T = O(min(σd√T + d‖θ‖, T‖θ‖)), so the worst case is O(dσ√T) with no log factor. The same paper proves a matching lower bound, which removes both the √d gap in d and the log^1.5 T gap in T. Caveat: the setting is tagged 'sparse', but no sparsity parameter is given, so I treated it as the dense unit-ball problem.

papers.title: Linear Bandits on Ellipsoids: Minimax Optimal Algorithms (Zhang, Hadiji, Combes)
papers.claim: For ellipsoid action sets including the unit ball, with noise that is subgaussian with variance proxy σ², E2TC achieves R_T ≤ 6dσ√T + lower-order terms, i.e. O(min(σd√T + d‖θ‖, T‖θ‖)) with no log factor. A matching lower bound Ω(min(dσ√T + d‖θ‖_A, ‖θ‖_A T)) makes this minimax optimal up to a universal constant.

papers.title: On the Minimax Regret for Linear Bandits in a wide variety of Action Spaces (Banerjee, Gopalan)
papers.claim: Proves a lower bound of d√n/(16√3) for ℓ_p balls with 1<p<∞. Follows the template of the unit-ball proof in Lattimore–Szepesvári Section 24.2 and notes that LinUCB attains the bound.

papers.title: Bandit Algorithms (Lattimore, Szepesvári), Theorem 24.2
papers.claim: Ω(d√n) regret lower bound for the unit-ball action set with Gaussian/subgaussian noise. Seen only as cited and restated by arXiv:2301.03597 and arXiv:2003.00153, not in the book itself.

papers.title: Stochastic Linear Bandits with Parameter Noise (Ezer, Cohen, Mansour)
papers.claim: States that in the classic additive-noise model the minimax regret on ℓ_p unit balls is of order d√T.

triage.summary: Under the reading that this is a finite realizable class F with |F| held fixed, the K and T gap is closed. EXP4 (Auer, Cesa-Bianchi, Freund, Schapire 2002) has expected regret O(sqrt(KT ln N)) against any N experts, including adversarial ones. I saw this attributed to Auer et al. in secondary sources (arXiv 2406.16802, 1508.03326) but did not open the 2002 paper itself. Taking the N <= |F| greedy policies induced by F gives O(sqrt(KT log|F|)), with no log T factor, for i.i.d. contexts and rewards in [0,1]. This matches the existing Omega(sqrt(KT)) lower bound, so the rate is Theta(sqrt(KT)). The log^{3/4} T factor in the recorded upper bounds, which come from SupLinUCB and Jin et al. 2026 and look like linear-model results with d=K, is therefore not needed. Agarwal et al. 2012 (arXiv 1202.1334, Thm 5.1) gives the matching realizable lower bound Omega(sqrt(KT ln N / ln K)). FALCON (Simchi-Levi & Xu, arXiv 2003.12699) reaches sqrt(KT log|F|) up to log terms with an efficient algorithm. Caveats: EXP4 is not computationally efficient. In |F| the bounds still differ by sqrt(log K). If the database means a different or infinite class, this conclusion does not carry over directly.

papers.title: The Nonstochastic Multiarmed Bandit Problem (EXP4)
papers.claim: Secondary sources attribute to Auer et al. an expected-regret bound of O(sqrt(KT ln N)) for EXP4 against any N experts, holding for any loss sequence. The bound's order was seen in search results, not checked in the original paper. With N <= |F| greedy policies under realizability, this gives O(sqrt(KT log|F|)) with no log T factor.

papers.title: Contextual Bandit Learning with Predictable Rewards
papers.claim: Theorem 5.1: for any algorithm there is a realizable function class of size at most N on which regret is Omega(sqrt(KT ln N / ln K)).

papers.title: Bypassing the Monster: A Faster and Simpler Optimal Algorithm for Contextual Bandits under Realizability
papers.claim: High-probability regret of order sqrt(KT log|F|) (up to log terms) under realizability with stochastic contexts, using an efficient algorithm (FALCON).

triage.summary: The gap is closed in K and T. Under realizability with a known finite class F, the greedy policies π_f(x) = argmax_a f(x,a) for f in F form at most |F| experts, and the optimal policy π_{f*} is one of them. Running EXP4 (Auer, Cesa-Bianchi, Freund, Schapire 2002) over these experts gives expected regret ≤ √(2TK ln|F|). This holds for any sequence of losses and expert advice, so it covers stochastic contexts. That is O(√(KT log|F|)) with no log T factor, i.e. Θ(√(KT)) when |F| is not tracked as a variable, as in this setting key. It matches the database's Ω(√(KT)) lower bounds up to constants; the log^0.75 T gap comes only from the database relying on regression-based upper bounds. Caveats: (i) EXP4's bound is in expectation only; Exp4.P (Beygelzimer et al. 2011) gives O(√(KT ln(|F|/δ))) with high probability. (ii) If |F| is tracked, Agarwal et al. (AISTATS 2012) give a realizable-setting lower bound. I recall it as Ω(√(KT log|F| / log K)) but did not verify that form; I only saw the abstract claim that realizability doesn't beat the agnostic rate in the worst case. If my recollection is right, a log K factor in the |F|-dependence may remain. (iii) The original 2002 EXP4 paper did not appear in my results; the √(2TK log N) constant is from Eldowa et al. (2023), and the order √(KT ln N) is confirmed by arXiv 2406.16802 and Beygelzimer et al.

papers.title: The Nonstochastic Multiarmed Bandit Problem (EXP4)
papers.claim: EXP4 achieves expected regret O(√(KT ln N)) against the best of N experts for any sequence of losses and expert advice; Eldowa et al. 2023 give the constant as √(2TK log N). Seen only through secondary sources (arXiv 2406.16802, Eldowa et al. ITW 2023). With the |F| greedy policies as experts, under realizability, this gives O(√(KT log|F|)) regret.

papers.title: Contextual Bandit Algorithms with Supervised Learning Guarantees (Exp4.P)
papers.claim: Exp4.P achieves O(√(KT ln(N/δ))) regret with high probability; the original Exp4 bound does not hold with high probability.

papers.title: Improved Regret Bounds for Bandits with Expert Advice
papers.claim: Restates that Auer et al. (2002) proved O(√(KT ln N)) expected regret for EXP4 as a worst-case result over any losses and expert recommendations.

papers.title: Contextual Bandit Learning with Predictable Rewards
papers.claim: Regressor Elimination under realizability achieves regret comparable to the agnostic setting. The paper also proves a lower bound showing realizability does not improve the worst case.

triage.summary:
The √log K gap is closed, but only by combining two published results. I did not find a paper that states the contextual bound itself.

Setting: M_ctx finite contexts chosen by an oblivious adversary, K arms, rewards in [0,1]. The database upper bound, √(2·K·M·T·log K), comes from running a separate Exp3 for each context.

**Upper bound without the log factor.** Replace Exp3 with Tsallis-INF (Zimmert & Seldin, arXiv 1807.07623). Its Theorem 1 bounds adversarial pseudo-regret by 4√(KT)+1 with importance-weighted estimators. The bound is anytime: the learning rate is η_t = 2/√t, so it needs neither T nor a doubling scheme. That matters here because each context's round count T_c is unknown in advance. Running one copy per context gives regret at most Σ_c(4√(K·T_c)+1). By Cauchy–Schwarz this is at most 4√(K·M·T)+M, which is O(√(KMT)) when T ≥ M. Against an oblivious adversary, pseudo-regret and expected regret coincide. Audibert & Bubeck's INF (COLT 2009 / JMLR 2010) already removed the √log K factor for the non-contextual problem.

**Matching lower bound.** Split the rounds into M blocks of T/M, one block per context, and apply the existing √((K−1)T)/504 bound to each block. This gives Ω(√(MKT)). Note that the lower bounds in the database omit the M factor.

So the minimax rate is Θ(√(KMT)): it is tight in K, M and T up to constants.

**Caveats.**
- I found no paper that explicitly states the composed O(√(KMT)) bound for this setting.
- I could not read the text of Lattimore & Szepesvári Chapter 18 ("One bandit per context"). The fetched PDF came back as unreadable binary, so I could not check whether the book makes this remark or poses it as an exercise.
- Neither of the two composition steps is spelled out in a paper I found. The anytime per-context argument and the block-splitting lower bound are my own reasoning. They are standard arguments, but I have not seen them written down this session.

papers.title: Tsallis-INF: An Optimal Algorithm for Stochastic and Adversarial Bandits (Zimmert, Seldin; JMLR 2021)
papers.claim: Theorem 1: anytime adversarial pseudo-regret ≤ 4√(KT)+1 (IW estimators), learning rate η_t=2/√t, no horizon knowledge needed. Running one copy per context gives O(√(KMT)), removing the √log K factor.

papers.title: Minimax Policies for Adversarial and Stochastic Bandits (Audibert, Bubeck; COLT 2009) / Regret Bounds and Minimax Policies under Partial Monitoring (JMLR 2010)
papers.claim: INF with a polynomial ψ removes the extraneous log factor in the adversarial bandit pseudo-regret, giving the minimax rate Θ(√(KT)) for non-contextual bandits.

triage.summary:
The log gap appears to be closed for finite realizable function classes. Foster & Rakhlin (ICML 2020, arXiv 2002.04926) prove that SquareCB has high-probability regret at most 4√(KT·Reg_Sq(T)) + O(√(KT log(2/δ))), with adversarial contexts allowed. For a finite class, Vovk's aggregating forecaster gives Reg_Sq(T) ≤ 2 log|F|. Section 1.2 of the paper says SquareCB then "enjoys the optimal rate" of order √(KT log|F|).

Expected regret is my own derivation, not a stated theorem. Integrating the √(log(1/δ)) tail gives an expected regret of O(√(KT log|F|) + √(KT)). If log|F| is held constant, that is O(√(KT)) with no polylog(T) factor. This matches the database's Ω(√(KT)) lower bound in both K and T. The database's upper bounds (√(KT)·log^{3/4}-type, and the √(KT log³) SupLinUCB bound) are therefore loose for this setting.

Caveat: the database's function_class field is empty. If the intended class is infinite or nonparametric, rates instead depend on the class's complexity. That case is covered by the paper's Theorem 2 lower bound, of order T^((1+p)/(2+p)) up to log factors when the class's entropy grows as ε^(-p).

Tool note: I couldn't parse the PDF, so I read the arXiv HTML version. I did not check the Agarwal et al. 2012 lower bound in log|F| during this session.

papers.title: Beyond UCB: Optimal and Efficient Contextual Bandits with Regression Oracles
papers.claim: SquareCB: Reg_CB(T) ≤ 4√(KT·Reg_Sq(T)) + O(√(KT log(2/δ))) w.h.p. with adversarial contexts under realizability. For finite F, Vovk aggregation gives Reg_Sq ≤ 2 log|F|, so regret is O(√(KT log|F|)), which the paper calls the optimal rate; with log|F| fixed this is √(KT) with no log T factor, matching the Ω(√(KT)) lower bound.

triage.summary:
The setting doesn't name a function class (function_class is empty and the reward model is marked "misspecified"), so this verdict depends on how I read it. The two upper bounds in the database come from linear contextual bandit results applied with dimension d = K: SupLinUCB (Chu et al. 2011) and jin2026nearly. The jin2026 paper I found is probably "Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linear Contextual Bandits with Arbitrary Adaptive Action Sets" (arXiv 2609.15170). I only saw its abstract in a search summary and did not confirm its author list or Corollary 18. Under the d = K reading, the gap is closed up to iterated-log factors by Li, Wang & Zhou (COLT 2019, arXiv 1904.00242). The search result summarising their abstract says:
- Lower bound: any algorithm suffers Ω(√(dT log T log n)) regret when there are n ≤ 2^{d/2} actions per round.
- Upper bound: their Variable-Confidence-Level SupLinUCB matches that lower bound up to iterated-log factors. This removes two √log T factors from the SupLinUCB analysis, which is exactly the source of the log^{3/2} T term in the database's upper bound.

With d = n = K (so the condition K ≤ 2^{K/2} holds for K ≥ 2), the minimax rate is about √(KT log T log K), up to log log factors. Two consequences: the database's √(KT) lower bound is loose by a √(log T log K) factor, and the T-exponent gap (log^{0.75}) is closed except for iterated logs. The K exponent is 1/2 on both sides, which matches.

Caveat: this only holds if the intended setting is K-armed linear contextual bandits with dimension about K. Under an unspecified general or misspecified function class, the right rate would depend on the class. For example, a finite class of size N gives √(KT log N) via Exp4-type algorithms, which I did not check against a source in this session, and the answer could change.

papers.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linearly Parameterized Bandits (Yingkai Li, Yining Wang, Yuan Zhou)
papers.claim: With dimension d and n ≤ 2^{d/2} actions per round, the minimax expected regret is Ω(√(dT log T log n)). VCL SupLinUCB matches this up to iterated-log factors, saving two √log T factors over the earlier SupLinUCB analysis.

papers.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linear Contextual Bandits with Arbitrary Adaptive Action Sets
papers.claim: Õ(K^{1/4}√(dT)) upper bound for 2 ≤ K ≤ d, with a matching lower bound up to logs when T ≥ d². Probably the source of the database's jin2026nearly upper bound, which gives K^{3/4}√T up to logs once d = K.

triage.summary: The setting is ambiguous as encoded. With finitely many stochastic contexts (M_ctx, distribution known), K arms, no function class and no structural extras, the minimax lower bound is Omega(sqrt(M_ctx K T)) when rewards depend arbitrarily on the context; that is the standard no-cross-learning bound restated by Balseiro et al. Then the stored lower bound sqrt(KT) is too weak and the stored upper bounds (which have no M_ctx term) don't apply. The bounds only make sense under hidden structure. (a) Cross-learning, the most likely reading because known M_ctx and known context distribution is the Balseiro et al. 2019 setup. There the search summary gives O(sqrt(KT log K)) for UCB1.CL with stochastic rewards; the abstract claims only Õ(sqrt(KT)) for a known context distribution. Follow-ups (Schneider-Zimmert 2023, arXiv 2401.01857; Huang-Huang, arXiv 2410.04080) also prove only Õ(sqrt(KT)), for adversarial losses with an unknown context distribution. I found no log-free bound and no explicit statement that the gap is open. (b) Contexts don't affect rewards (e.g. linear with fixed one-hot features, which is how SupLinUCB with d=K applies). Then MOSS (Audibert-Bubeck 2009) gets O(sqrt(KT)), matching Auer et al. 2002, and the gap is closed. One search summary credits MOSS to Lai (1987); most sources credit Audibert and Bubeck. Recommended fixes: add a cross-learning flag to 'extras' if that is intended. The per-variable K exponent of 0.5 doesn't match the stored jin2026nearly bound, which grows like K^{3/4} up to logs. I couldn't find the jin2026nearly paper.

papers.title: Contextual Bandits with Cross-learning
papers.claim: With cross-learning, the abstract claims Õ(sqrt(KT)) regret for stochastic contexts with a known distribution; per the search summary, UCB1.CL gets O(sqrt(KT log K)) for stochastic rewards; without cross-learning, Omega(sqrt(CKT)) is necessary.

papers.title: Optimal cross-learning for contextual bandits with unknown context distributions
papers.claim: Nearly tight Õ(sqrt(KT)) regret (up to log factors) for cross-learning with adversarial losses and i.i.d. contexts from an unknown distribution, in expectation.

papers.title: High Probability Bound for Cross-Learning Contextual Bandits with Unknown Context Distributions
papers.claim: High-probability Õ(sqrt(KT)) bound for cross-learning contextual bandits with unknown context distributions.

papers.title: A minimax and asymptotically optimal algorithm for stochastic bandits
papers.claim: Discusses MOSS (Audibert-Bubeck) attaining minimax-optimal O(sqrt(KT)) regret for K-armed stochastic bandits.

triage.summary: Closed as a function of K and T: regret is Θ(√(KT)) with no log T factor; with the class size N (not tracked in our key) the rates become √(KT·ln N). The log T factors in our upper bounds come from linear-bandit results (SupLinUCB; Jin et al. Cor. 18). For a realizable finite class F with |F| = N, run Exp4 (Auer et al. 2002) on the N greedy policies π_f(x) = argmax_a f(x,a). It gets expected regret O(√(KT ln N)) with no log T, even against adversaries; the 2110.13282 citation calls this optimal, and Lattimore's 2018 slides tune it to √(2nk log m). Exp4.P (Beygelzimer et al. 2011) gets O(√(KT ln N)) with high probability. For fixed N this matches the Ω(√(KT)) lower bound in our database. Agarwal et al. 2012 studies exactly this realizable, known-context-distribution setting. It proves O(√(KT ln(NT/δ))) for Regressor Elimination and a lower bound of Ω(√(KT ln N / ln K)) over realizable classes. So even with N tracked, only a √(ln K) gap remains. Not verified: I could not fetch the Exp4 theorem text from Lattimore–Szepesvári Ch. 18 or Auer et al. 2002 directly; that claim rests on the secondary sources above.

triage.summary:
The gap in d is closed by a known result. The remaining gap in T is only logarithmic.

**The d gap.** The database's lower bounds are √(Td). These come from multi-armed or adversarial bandit constructions, so they are weak in d. Lattimore & Szepesvári (Bandit Algorithms, 2020, Ch. 24, hypercube theorem) prove an Ω(d√T) minimax lower bound for stochastic linear bandits with Gaussian noise. The construction uses actions in [-1,1]^d and parameters in {±1/√T}^d. In that construction the optimal arms are the 2^d corners. I believe the same argument goes through when the action set is just the finite set {-1,1}^d. Zhou, Gu & Szepesvári (2012.08507) use exactly that finite hypercube {-1,1}^{d-1} as a linear-bandit lower bound. A finite action set with a fixed bound on action norms is allowed, and the parameter set is unbounded, so rescaling to norm L costs nothing. This makes the lower bound Ω(d√T) in the finite-action setting. That matches the d-exponent 1 of the upper bound (Dani et al. 2008 give O(d√T·polylog T); OFUL and finite-arm phase elimination give the same rate). So the poly gap in d is closed at d√T.

**The T gap.** A gap of polylog(T) remains between d√T and d√T·polylog T. This is a log factor only, and I did not find a paper that closes it for finite action sets of unbounded size.

**Caveats.**
- The secondary sources I found describe the theorem as stated for [-1,1]^d. Applying it to the finite corner set is my own argument from the proof structure, not something I saw stated.
- I could not read the book text: fetching the PDF returned only binary. The theorem statement is confirmed only through citing papers (2105.10590 and 2603.03843 in search snippets).
- I also could not read the PDF of 2012.08507, so its {-1,1}^{d-1} claim comes from a search-result snippet only.

For fixed compact action sets the worst-case lower bound is Ω(d√T), shown by Rusmevichientong & Tsitsiklis (2010) for the unit sphere/ball. Zhang–Hadiji–Combes (2025) cite it, plus a more general Assouad-style version in the Lattimore–Szepesvári book. This matches the d-dependence of the d√T·polylog(T) upper bounds (Dani et al. 2008; OFUL), so d is tight. Caveat: these lower bounds use Gaussian noise. The standard swap to Bernoulli rewards with means near 1/2 should give the same bound up to constants for rewards in [0,1], but I did not see it stated explicitly. What remains is a log-T-type gap (polylog(T) upper bound vs Ω(d√T) lower bound) for arbitrary compact sets. Zhang–Hadiji–Combes (2025) remove the log factors for ellipsoids, getting minimax-optimal Θ(dσ√T) up to a universal constant. I found no result that does this for general compact sets, and no paper stating it as an open problem; I could not see the Chapter 24 notes of the Lattimore–Szepesvári book. Li–Wang–Zhou (2019) prove Ω(√(dT log T log n)) for n ≤ 2^{d/2} actions per round, but the abstract's wording suggests the action sets can change between rounds, so it doesn't directly apply to this fixed-set setting. triage.summary:
I found no published result that closes this gap. The gap itself is stated explicitly in the paper that gives the upper bound. One label in the database seems to be wrong.

**Where the upper bound comes from.** The cited upper bound, bai2021sample Theorem 5, is Bai, Jin, Wang & Xiong, "Sample-Efficient Learning of Stackelberg Equilibria in General-Sum Games" (NeurIPS 2021, arXiv 2102.11494). I read the theorem list in the ar5iv version. Theorem 5 is not about K-armed bandits. It is an Õ(d²/ε²) upper bound for learning Stackelberg equilibria in linear bandit games, where d is the feature dimension. The database appears to have recorded d as "K".

**The gap is acknowledged in the same paper.** Appendix E.2 adapts the paper's bandit-game lower bound to get Ω(d/ε²) for linear bandit games. The authors say the upper bound is off from this "by at most an Õ(d) factor". That is the K² (really d²) versus K (really d) gap in the database.

**What I could not find.**
- No later paper in my searches tightens the linear-bandit Stackelberg rate to d/ε² or raises the lower bound to d²/ε².
- I could not identify li2023tight, the claimed source of the lower bound. In any case, Bai et al. already give an Ω(d/ε²) lower bound for this setting.
- I could not find a formal statement calling this an open problem. It is "known open" only in the sense that the authors explicitly flag the gap.

**If you meant the plain finite-action setting.** For the setting the database labels as K-armed (finite action sets, bandit feedback), the same paper is tight. Theorem 2 gives an Õ(AB/ε²) upper bound and Theorem 3 a matching Ω(AB/ε²) lower bound, where A and B are the two players' action counts. If the intended setting is a Stackelberg bandit game with A = B = K, the gap is closed at K²/ε².

**Checking limits.** The PDF fetches returned unreadable binary, so I took the theorem statements from the ar5iv HTML version. That page's answer covered only the first 100k of its 185k characters, but the theorem list and the Appendix E.2 remark were both readable there.

triage.summary:
**Verdict: closed.** The gap your database flags comes mainly from a lower bound that is too weak. The published literature already gives a matching lower bound for this setting, and in the main case (ellipsoid action sets, including the unit ball) the log factor is also gone.

**The d gap.** The √(dT) lower bounds in your database are the generic ones for finite-armed or simplex-type problems. Rusmevichientong & Tsitsiklis (2010), Theorem 2.1, prove a stronger bound for arms on the unit sphere with Gaussian noise. Under a N(0, I/d) prior on θ, any policy has Bayes risk at least 0.006·d·√T when T ≥ d². So some fixed θ has regret Ω(d√T). The Lattimore–Szepesvári book also gives an Ω(d√T) bound for the unit ball, as reported in a search-result summary of arXiv 2502.17175; I did not read the book. The Dani et al. (2008) upper bound is about d√T·polylog(T), so the dependence on d is matched.

**The log factor in T.** Zhang, Hadiji & Combes (2025, arXiv 2502.17175) handle ellipsoidal action sets {x : xᵀA⁻¹x ≤ 1}, which are strongly convex and include the unit ball. They prove a lower bound of Ω(min(dσ√T + d‖θ‖_A, ‖θ‖_A·T)). Their algorithm estimates ‖θ‖ and then explores and commits, and it matches this bound up to a universal constant. That gives minimax Θ(d√T) with no logarithms.

Rusmevichientong & Tsitsiklis's PEGE algorithm also achieves a log-free d√T on any strongly convex set, but its bound carries a factor (‖θ‖ + 1/‖θ‖). It is therefore not a uniform worst-case bound when θ may be near zero, as it is here.

**Caveat.** I found no log-free uniform worst-case upper bound for arbitrary strongly convex sets beyond ellipsoids. For that wider class the confirmed rate is Ω(d√T) against O(d√T·polylog T). So the polynomial gap in d is closed outright, and the remaining log gap in T is closed for ellipsoids and balls. I am fairly confident in these claims; my searches were not exhaustive. Two papers I saw in results but did not read are Kerdreux et al. (arXiv 2103.05907) on uniformly convex sets and a Thompson-sampling result on the ball (arXiv 2410.16013).

**Sources**
- [Linearly Parameterized Bandits – arXiv 0812.3465](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3465) (ar5iv version used for theorem details)
- [Linearly Parameterized Bandits – MIT PDF](https://www.mit.edu/~jnt/Papers/J129-10-linearBandit.pdf)
- [Linearly Parameterized Bandits – INFORMS (Math. of OR)](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/moor.1100.0446)
- [Linear Bandits on Ellipsoids: Minimax Optimal Algorithms – arXiv 2502.17175](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.17175)
- [Linear Bandits on Uniformly Convex Sets – arXiv 2103.05907](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.05907)
- [Information-Theoretic Minimax Regret Bounds for RL based on Duality – arXiv 2410.16013](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.16013)

Theorem 3.1: on SBAR(J) action sets (equivalent to strong convexity; covers balls and ellipsoids), PEGE has regret ≤ a1(‖z‖ + 1/‖z‖)·r√T with no log factor. Theorem 4.1: on general compact sets, the UE policy has regret O(r√T·log^{3/2} T).
